CALL AND NOTICE OF SPECIAL MEETING

To the Members of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates:

NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN that the Mayor has called a Special Meeting of the City Council to be
called to order in the Council Chambers of City Hall, located at 340 Palos Verdes Dr. West, Palos Verdes
Estates, CA at 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, April 24, 2018. The agenda for the special meeting with the items
of business to be transacted or discussed is set forth below.

Posted by the Office of the City Clerk on Friday, April 20, 2018, at 5:00 p.m.

  April 24, 2018
  5:00 P.M.
  Council Chambers of City Hall
  340 Palos Verdes Dr. West
  Palos Verdes Estates

  AGENDA
  OF A SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to
on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If
applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the
agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s office during normal business hours.
Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry
concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made
available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans
with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting
to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.

The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to
allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation
shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to
fill out a green speaker’s card available at the end of each row in the Chambers. The card permits the
City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. The City Council, at the
direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the
agenda.

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

FROM:  ANTON DAHLERBRUCH, CITY MANAGER /s/

SUBJECT: DISCUSSION OF MATRIX CONSULTING GROUP STUDY
  ENTITLED “ASSESSMENT OF NON-SAFETY CITY FUNCTIONS”
  IN REFERENCE TO ORGANIZATION OPERATION, STRUCTURE,
  AND SERVICE EFFICIENCIES AND RECOMMENDATIONS

DATE:  APRIL 24, 2018

ISSUE/PURPOSE

The City Council commissioned the Matrix Consulting Group to evaluate and recommend
efficiencies, improvements, and cost saving for the City’s non-safety functions. At the City
Council meeting on March 13, 2018, the Matrix “Organizational Assessment of Non-Safety
Functions” report was presented by Alan Pennington for review and discussion. The City
Council received the report and public input, and called for workshop to further consider the
recommendations and City Management input. The purpose of this report is to transmit the
input of City Management for the City Council’s consideration and deliberation of the
recommendations in the Organizational Assessment of Non-Safety Functions study.

BACKGROUND

At the City Council meeting on October 30, 2017, per the recommendation of the Ad Hoc
Committee consisting of Mayor Pro Tem Peterson and Council Member King in consultation
with Treasurer Lozzi, the City Council approved an agreement with the Matrix Consulting
Group for:

  conducting an analysis and evaluation of service delivery options, opportunities for
  efficiencies and operational improvements, organization structure and staffing, and
  budgetary needs for Building, Safety, Planning, Public Works, Parkland Maintenance,
  and Administrative Services including the Finance Department, City Clerk’s Office and
  City Manager’s Office.

  Page 1 of 3

  001
 The study was also directed to incorporate:

1. Input from, and potentially involvement by, interested residents,
2. Policy recommendations for City Council consideration,
3. Management/administrative recommendations for the City Manager. A comparison of the
  cost of the services presently delivered by HR Green to the costs of the same services as if
  City employees delivered the services;
4. For major contracts (building and safety services, engineering services, tree trimming and
  landscape maintenance), an assessment of contractor costs (rates) charged to the City of
  Palos Verdes Estates in relation to similar contractor charges of comparable cities.
5. Justification and recommendations for the balance and configuration between in-house
  and contract services specifying suggested titles of recommended in-house positions, an
  outline of job duties and responsibilities, and suggested salary ranges for all in-house
  services in relation to recommended contract service functions.
6. Recommendations for modifications to the contract(s) for outsourced services.
7. Independent overview of City financial documents and budget for reasonableness in
  comparison to similar cities.
8. Comparative information from similar cities of staffing levels, budget, and service delivery
  structure.

The Ad Hoc Committee, with the Treasurer, convened several times to receive progress reports
from the Matrix Consulting Group. Independent of City influence or input into the Matrix
Consulting Group conclusions and recommendations, the final report was presented to the City
Council at its meeting on March 13, 2018.

DISCUSSION

City Management has reviewed the Organizational Assessment of Non-Safety Functions
study. Staff has no objections to the recommendations and does not find glaring inaccuracies
in the report.

Attached is the summary list of recommendations with City Management comments and
alternatives. In reference to a majority of the recommendations, it is staff’s observation that
there would be a financial (staffing or consultant) cost to implement them. In reference to the
recommendation for a receptionist and changing to a contract for urban forestry, both will have
a service-level impact for consideration of the cost and benefit.

On April 24, 2018, approximately 45 minutes has been scheduled for the City Council’s
discussion of the study and City Management comments. Mr. Pennington will be on the
speaker telephone to participate in the meeting. It is recommended that the City Council
initially discuss the five major recommendations of the study. In no particular order, they are:

•  Code Enforcement Officer
•  Urban Forester
•  Part-Time Receptionist
•  Documents on the City website
•  Performance Standards

  Page 2 of 3

  002
 Staff will be available to participate in the discussion of these items and any others that are
specifically considered.

At the conclusion of the discussion, it is requested that the City Council provide direction.
Some of the options include, and are not limited to:

1. Continue the discussion to another meeting; determine a date and time.
2. Provide direction for recommendations to be included in the budget process, either in the
  base budget or as a “decision package” for prioritization and discussion with other budget
  matters.
3. Direct immediate implementation of an action.
4. Take no action.

FISCAL IMPACT

There is no fiscal impact with review and discussion of the Organizational Assessment of Non-
Safety Functions study.

NOTIFICATION

The agenda and the staff reports for this meeting were posted and noticed as required.

CONCLUSION/RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council receive public input on this agenda item. Then, it is
suggested that the City Council determine the specific recommendations within the
Organizational Assessment of Non-Safety Functions study to discuss. Thereafter, it is
suggested that Mr. Pennington to provide a brief overview of each identified recommendation,
staff provide comments, and the City Council deliberate and provide direction.
